info.name: 3PL Automation - Logic Apps
info.description:
Requests for the Request-triggered Logic Apps (Standard) workflows in three3pllogicapp: the 5 config-delivery workflows (btp-config-publish, mulesoft-config-generation, mulesoft-config-publish, solace-config-generation, solace-config-publish), the onboarding pipeline entry points (data-enrichment, enrichment-status, onboarding-launcher, onboarding-orchestrator), and request-branch-approval-via-email (the async, e-mail-based replacement for the old Teams-card branch-approval workflow).

**Not included here** — no HTTP trigger to test manually: data-enrichment-notifier (Recurrence), data-enrichment-mail-intake (new-mail trigger), approval-resume (Recurrence). To exercise those, actually submit incomplete data via data-enrichment / onboarding-launcher and reply to the real e-mails they send.

**Direction (Inbound/Outbound), new this pass:** data-enrichment now accepts a `direction` field per domain. `Outbound` (default) behaves exactly as before — a partial submission goes into the SME e-mail chase loop. `Inbound` skips that chase entirely: once required fields validate, EnrichmentStatus is set to Complete immediately on the same call.

**Architecture approval, new this pass:** onboarding-launcher now gates on a whole-onboarding architecture sign-off (table OnboardingApproval) *after* the enrichment gate and *before* invoking the orchestrator. First launch attempt for a correlationId returns 202 {status:'AwaitingArchitectureApproval'} and sends an e-mail — it does not invoke the orchestrator yet. The real approve/reject happens by replying to that e-mail (not testable via Postman); to actually see the orchestrator run in a Postman-only test, update OnboardingApproval.ArchitectureApprovalStatus to 'Approved' directly in SQL first.

**Local testing (default):** run the project with `func host start` (or F5 in VS Code with the Logic Apps Standard extension). The `baseUrl` collection variable defaults to `http://localhost:7071`, and no signature is required locally. The 3 new requests (onboarding-launcher, enrichment-status, request-branch-approval-via-email) use `{{baseUrl}}` + the `{{sig}}` collection variable so they work locally out of the box.

**Deployed/Azure testing:** set `baseUrl` to `https://<your-logic-app-name>.azurewebsites.net` and `sig` to that workflow's SAS signature (from the workflow's Callback URL in the Azure Portal) since Standard Logic App HTTP triggers are SAS-signed when hosted in Azure. The older requests in this collection have a real, already-committed prod URL+signature baked in from a previous pass — treat those as already-exposed and due for rotation, not a pattern to copy for new requests.

Note: `githubToken` for the mulesoft/solace publish workflows and TriggerBtpDeployment's `githubToken` are both read from the `githubToken` app setting on the server side (`appsetting('githubToken')`), not from the request body, so they are intentionally omitted from these request bodies.

request.description:
Fans out to only the domains listed in `domains` (default all 3 if omitted) — btp-config-publish, mulesoft-config-generation→mulesoft-config-publish, and/or solace-config-generation→solace-config-publish — each wrapped in its own Scope (Scope-BTP/Scope-MuleSoft/Scope-Solace) inside an outer Scope-Try/Scope-Catch. Do NOT send appYaml/devYaml/tstYaml/prodYaml under mulesoft.publish or solaceConfigJson under solace.publish — the orchestrator wires those in itself from the matching generate step's output. Only send the fields each generate/publish step actually needs from the caller (csvContent, repo/branch/path, commitMessage).

If a domain's GitHub feature branch doesn't exist yet, that domain's generation step now returns {status:'AwaitingBranchApproval'} instead of failing — the orchestrator treats this as a genuine third outcome (skips publish, does not throw), and the response's btp/mulesoft/solace sections will show it. This is not a bug if you see it in a test — it means request-branch-approval-via-email already sent an e-mail and the domain's SolaceClient/MuleSoftPartner row now has DeploymentStatus='AwaitingBranchApproval'.

On success returns 200 with {status, correlationId, domains, btp, mulesoft, solace}; on any child failure returns 500 with per-branch failure detail (result('Scope-Try') plus each domain's own result()).

Triggers a GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch (btp-Api-management-deploy.yml) via TriggerBtpDeployment. All body fields fall back to defaults baked into btp-config-publish/workflow.json if omitted; githubToken always comes from the server-side `githubToken` app setting.

request.description:
Builds app/dev/tst/prod.yaml from a MuleSoft NAV onboarding requirements CSV (long format, one row per RowType: Environment/TransactionType/MessageType/SourceDestination/UomMapping). Set updateExisting=true and populate existingAppYaml/existingDevYaml/existingTstYaml/existingProdYaml to merge incrementally instead of building fresh. See MuleSoftCsvParser.cs for the full column reference.

If the target branch doesn't exist yet, this workflow no longer blocks waiting for a Teams approval — it calls request-branch-approval-via-email (fire-and-forget), sets the domain row's DeploymentStatus='AwaitingBranchApproval', and immediately responds {status:'AwaitingBranchApproval', correlationId, branch} instead of the usual {status:'Complete', ...} body. That's expected, not an error, if you see it against a repo/branch combination that doesn't exist.

request.description: Commits non-blank appYaml/devYaml/tstYaml/prodYaml content to a GitHub feature branch under filePathPrefix (creating the branch from baseBranch if needed). Normally chained after 'MuleSoft Config Generation' in the real pipeline, but can be called standalone for testing. githubToken is not accepted in the body here (Logic App reads it from the githubToken app setting).

Generates Solace onboarding config JSON from a CSV batch (multiple Brand/Env/SystemName/ThreePLCode records per call, unlike MuleSoft's single-record CSV). Body defaults to the same sample CSV baked into solace-config-generation/workflow.json's coalesce() default. Can be omitted entirely to exercise that default.

If the target branch doesn't exist yet, this workflow no longer blocks waiting for a Teams approval — it calls request-branch-approval-via-email (fire-and-forget), sets the domain row's DeploymentStatus='AwaitingBranchApproval', and immediately responds {status:'AwaitingBranchApproval', correlationId, branch} instead of the usual {status:'Complete', ...} body. That's expected, not an error, if you see it against a repo/branch combination that doesn't exist.

Commits solaceConfigJson to a GitHub feature branch at filePath (creating the branch from baseBranch if needed). Normally chained after 'Solace Config Generation'; replace solaceConfigJson with real output from that call for an end-to-end test. githubToken is not accepted in the body here (Logic App reads it from the githubToken app setting).

request.description:
Single intake endpoint for all 3 domains (Btp/Solace/MuleSoft, set via `domain`). Upserts the parent row + replaces child rows, then recomputes EnrichmentStatus.

**`direction`** (new): 'Outbound' (default if omitted) behaves exactly as before — a partial submission with missing required fields is saved as EnrichmentStatus='AwaitingInput' and picked up by the SME e-mail chase loop. 'Inbound' skips that chase entirely: as long as the required fields for this domain validate on THIS call, EnrichmentStatus is set to 'Complete' immediately — nobody ever gets an enrichment e-mail for this row. Try changing this sample's direction to 'Inbound' and removing a required field to see the difference: Outbound → 200 {enrichmentStatus:'AwaitingInput'}, Inbound → 400 validation error instead (Inbound still requires completeness up front, it just doesn't chase gaps afterward).

Response: 200 {domain, correlationId, record, enrichmentStatus} · 400 on validation failure · 500 on error.

item.name: Onboarding Launcher (gated launch — enrichment gate then architecture-approval gate)

request.description:
Server-side gated launch. `domains` selects which domain(s) to launch — omit it to default to all 3 (['btp','solace','mulesoft']); pass a single-element array (e.g. ['solace']) to launch just that domain, reusing the same per-domain gate/CSV-build machinery.

Gate order: (1) enrichment gate — every requested domain must exist, be EnrichmentStatus='Complete', not already DeploymentStatus='InProgress', and not 'Deployed' unless forceRedeploy=true — fail here → 409 with per-domain reasons. (2) NEW architecture-approval gate — checks OnboardingApproval for this correlationId: not yet requested → inserts/resets it to Pending, sends the architecture-approval e-mail, and responds 202 {status:'AwaitingArchitectureApproval'} WITHOUT invoking the orchestrator; already Pending → 202 again, no duplicate e-mail; Approved → proceeds to invoke onboarding-orchestrator exactly as before.

To actually see it proceed past the architecture gate in a manual test (since the real approval happens by e-mail reply, not via Postman), UPDATE dbo.OnboardingApproval SET ArchitectureApprovalStatus='Approved' WHERE CorrelationId='test-solace-001' in SQL, then re-send this same request.

Responses: 202 {status:'OrchestrationStarted', correlationId, domains} once actually launched · 202 {status:'AwaitingArchitectureApproval', ...} while gated · 409 {error, domains} on enrichment-gate failure · 500 on error.

item.name: Enrichment Status (read-only aggregate — incl. Direction and approval states)

request.description:
Read-only poll target for the UI's Status view — safe to call repeatedly. `includeDetail` (new): false/omitted returns the light response — per domain (btp/solace/mulesoft): {found, enrichmentStatus, deploymentStatus, direction, missingFields[]}, plus {branchApprovalStatus, pendingBranchName} on solace/mulesoft only. true returns the full response, adding a `record` object per domain (every enriched field), a top-level `common` section (the Onboarding/interface row), and MuleSoft's child arrays (environments, transactionTypes, messageTypes, sourceDestinations, uomMappings) and Solace's messageTypes. Both variants also return a top-level {architectureApproval: {status, approverEmail, respondedAt}} for the whole onboarding (not per domain), `readyToLaunch` (all 3 found and Complete), and the masked audit trail (TOP 100, ActorEmail masked in T-SQL — EncryptedPassword is never selected by this or any other read path).

Response: 200 {correlationId, readyToLaunch, architectureApproval, btp, solace, mulesoft, auditTrail} · 400 if correlationId is missing · 500 on error.

item.name: Request Branch Approval Via Email (async — renamed from request-feature-branch-via-teams)

request.description:
Normally invoked by solace-config-generation/mulesoft-config-generation when Check_Branch_Exists finds the target branch missing — called standalone here for testing. `domain` must be 'Solace' or 'MuleSoft' (selects which table gets updated).

Unlike the old Teams-card version, this **cannot block** waiting for a decision (there is no webhook to wait on) — it sends the approval e-mail (or skips sending if BranchApprovalStatus is already 'Pending', to avoid duplicates), sets BranchApprovalStatus='Pending', PendingBranchName, and DeploymentStatus='AwaitingBranchApproval' on the domain row, audits BranchApprovalRequested, and responds immediately. The actual approve/reject happens later by e-mail reply to data-enrichment-mail-intake (subject tag [Approval: <id>|Branch-Solace]), which flips BranchApprovalStatus only — the approval-resume poller (recurrence, not HTTP-testable) is what actually re-launches the domain afterward.

Response: 200 {status:'AwaitingBranchApproval', correlationId, branchName} · 500 on error.
